one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration app with public REST API and MCP server

evidence.claim: Pumble apps authenticate via OAuth2 with consent screen, scopes, and access tokens
evidence.quote: Pumble uses OAuth2 in order to allow your app to access the API.

evidence.claim: Workspace users can self-serve generate API keys via the API addon for simple HTTP requests
evidence.quote: This addon lets you generate an API key that allows you to send messages, reactions, and more via simple HTTP requests.

evidence.claim: API key addon is available to all roles on all plans, including free
evidence.quote:
Who can use this feature?

Owner, Admin, Member

evidence.claim: Public REST API covering users, channels, and messages, authenticated via token and x-app-token headers
evidence.quote: Built on REST principles, this API allows you to integrate Pumble into your own app, by using the endpoints below.

evidence.claim: Pumble provides an official MCP server for connecting third-party AI agents
evidence.quote: With the Pumble Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, you can connect third-party AI agents (e.g., Claude, Gemini, Codex) to Pumble

notes: Official MCP server at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp (HTTP transport, authenticated with token + x-app-token headers); MCP tool set is dynamic based on app scopes. Unusual dual-header auth: every API request needs both 'token' (user/bot access token) and 'x-app-token' (app key prefixed 'xpat-'). Rate limits: 100 req/min per user token, 500 req/min per app on main API; API addon allows up to 1000 req/min per user. Official Node SDK (pumble-sdk) and CLI (npx pumble-cli login) exist; apps are created from workspace settings (Create app) or via manifest API. API addon key flow is narrower (messages, reactions, channel listing) than full OAuth2 app flow.
